problem: Embodied AI simulators and benchmarks focused almost entirely on navigation, or on high-level 'magic' object interactions such as invoking an 'open' command. Manipulation environments (Meta-World, RLBench, SAPIEN, RoboTurk) were mostly static table-top setups with few objects and little visual complexity. No visually rich, physics-enabled platform existed for joint mobile navigation plus low-level arm manipulation that also tests generalization to unseen scenes and objects.
motivation: Navigation is a means to an end: the goal is agents that act on objects, and near-perfect learned PointNav agents make it a natural time to move toward manipulation. Mobile manipulation adds challenges PointNav lacks: the agent's shape changes with the arm, obstacles must be avoided in 3D clutter, the arm and object occlude the view, and multi-phase planning is needed. Simulating this requires fine-grained collision checking and physics at usable frame rates.
key_idea: Add an IK-driven arm with an abstracted sphere grasper to AI2-THOR (ManipulaTHOR) and define ArmPointNav, a PointNav-style mobile pick-and-place task where source and goal are given as relative 3D coordinates, with a baseline end-to-end DD-PPO agent.
insight: Standard PointNav-style end-to-end RL transfers only partially: pickup is fairly easy (PuSR 89.9%), but carrying the object to the goal without disturbing the scene is hard (SRwD 39.4%). Sharing one policy across the pickup and move-to-goal phases is essential. A disjoint two-policy model reaches a higher PuSR (91.6) but 0.0 SR, because the second policy only gets gradients from episodes with a successful pickup. Vision matters even with perfect relative coordinates (No-Vision SRwD 10.3 vs 39.4), and depth alone beats RGB (21.2) and RGBD (37.1). Generalizing to novel object categories is harder than generalizing to novel scenes: SeenScenes-NovelObj SRwD of 32.2 is about the same as Test-NovelObj's 32.7.
method: ManipulaTHOR arm: a 3-joint equal-limb arm inspired by Kinova, all swivel joints, max reach a 0.6335 m hemisphere, height adjustable along the body; driven by inverse kinematics from the wrist position or by forward kinematics joint-by-joint.

Abstracted grasper: a sphere at the end of the arm with adjustable radius; any object intersecting it can be picked up (following the rearrangement 'abstracted grasping' model), with a drop action; NVIDIA PhysX via Unity for collisions and force cascades; about 300 fps training on 8×T4 GPUs.

ArmPointNav task and APND dataset: 30 AI2-THOR kitchens (20 train / 5 val / 5 test) and 12 pickupable target categories (6 seen in training, 6 novel); source and goal are given as (x,y,z) in the agent frame; about 72k valid object locations; evaluation uses 60 sampled tasks per object per scene; metrics are SRwD, SR, PuSR, Len, SuLen, PuLen.

Policy network: 3 conv layers + FC give a 512-d visual embedding of the depth (or RGB/RGBD) frame; 2 FC+ReLU layers embed the relative arm→object and arm→goal coordinates into 512-d; both are concatenated into a GRU (hidden size 512) with actor and critic heads.

Action space: 13 discrete actions: move forward 20 cm, rotate ±45°, move the wrist ±5 cm along x/y/z relative to the agent, raise/lower the arm height by 7 cm, abstract grasp, and Done; maximum episode length 200.
Training: DD-PPO in AllenAct for 20M frames; reward r_t = 10·I_success + 5·I_pickup + Δ(arm→object distance) + Δ(object→goal distance).

numbers_note: Only test-scene and seen-scene results are reported; no validation-split numbers. The ablation table (Table 2) does not state its split; its Depth row is identical to Test-SeenObj in Table 1. A No-Vision ablation (GPS only) gives SRwD 10.3, PuSR 66.8, SR 18.7, PuLen 38.1, SuLen 65.6, Len 64.9 and is omitted from 'numbers' because of the variant cap. SRwD as a function of initial distance to goal is shown only in a figure (Fig. 7). There are no external baselines; all comparisons are the authors' own ablations.
results: The depth-based end-to-end DD-PPO agent reaches 39.4% SRwD / 68.7% SR / 89.9% PuSR on Test-SeenObj and 32.7% SRwD / 62.1% SR on Test-NovelObj. It beats its own ablations: No-Vision (10.3 SRwD), RGB (21.2), RGBD (37.1) and a disjoint two-policy model (0.0 SR despite 91.6 PuSR). The large gap between pickup success and disturbance-free success shows that PointNav-style methods leave substantial room for improvement on mobile manipulation.
limitations: Grasping is abstracted as a sphere-intersection 'magic' pickup; there is no realistic gripper or grasp planning, and objects inside receptacles (e.g. a closed microwave or fridge) are excluded.
The agent relies on perfect relative 3D coordinates of arm-to-object and arm-to-goal every step; there is no noisy or learned localization, and evaluation is only in simulation.
The benchmark covers only 30 kitchen scenes and 12 object categories; there are no external baselines, and the ablation table does not state its split.
builds_on: abstracted grasping from Rearrangement (Batra et al. 2020)
